**Reference:** *Mathematics for Machine Learning* (2020), Chapter 8, §8.5. This tutorial uses independent wording, derivations and order data.

## The question we need to answer

A probabilistic dependency graph separates a system's factorisation assumptions from the physical dependency graph of microservices. A directed edge encodes a conditional relation in a model.

## Formal relationship

$$
p(D,N,T)=p(D)p(N\mid D)p(T\mid D,N)
$$

The notation makes the assumptions and dependencies explicit. Check that the variables, sets and dimensions match the running example before drawing a conclusion.

## Derive the answer from the example

Let D be route distance, N item count, T fulfilment time. In this illustrative DAG, distance influences the item-count distribution and both condition the time. Multiplying the conditional factors reconstructs a joint model that can be sampled or queried.

## Interpretation and limitations

Graphical arrows are not automatically causal; the factorisation alone does not prove that intervening on D would change T in a particular way. Missing edges encode conditional independence assumptions.

## Explain it yourself

If distance and item count are assumed independent, how would the joint factorisation change?
